images.filename: Spanish-American War Cannon; Univ of Tampa-1.JPG
images.caption: The former Fort Dade Spanish-American War era cannon on the grounds of the Henry B. Plant Museum/Tampa Bay Hotel on the grounds of the University of Tampa. Further details to come later. Note: The gun is an 8-inch M1888 coast defense gun, the same model as the original one from Fort Dade, but is on a railway mounting dismounted from the railcar, and was previously at Fort Morgan, Alabama. The gun mentioned on the monument was on a disappearing carriage and was donated to a World War II scrap drive.
images.alt: The former Fort Dade Spanish-American War era cannon on the grounds of the Henry B. Plant Museum/Tampa Bay Hotel on the grounds of the University of Tampa. Further details to come later. Note: The gun is an 8-inch M1888 coast defense gun, the same model as the original one from Fort Dade, but is on a railway mounting dismounted from the railcar, and was previously at Fort Morgan, Alabama. The gun mentioned on the monument was on a disappearing carriage and was donated to a World War II scrap drive.

images.caption: Built in 1891 by Henry B Plant at a cost of. $2.5 Million, plus another $500,00 for furnishings, is located at 401 W Kennedy Blouvard in Tampa, Florida..  It is noted for it’s famous Moorish design featuring the silver colored Minarets.  Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in Tampa, Florida #72000322.It is currently the home of the University of Tampa, and the H.B. Plant Museum.
images.alt: Built in 1891 by Henry B Plant at a cost of. $2.5 Million, plus another $500,00 for furnishings, is located at 401 W Kennedy Blouvard in Tampa, Florida..  It is noted for it’s famous Moorish design featuring the silver colored Minarets.  Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in Tampa, Florida #72000322.It is currently the home of the University of Tampa, and the H.B. Plant Museum.

images.caption: The Henry Bradley Plant Memorial Fountain and its statue named "Transportation." It is located at the entrance to Plant Park. The ship and train in the sculpture represent Plant's system of railroads and steamship lines. The eagle holding the strongbox is the logo of The Southern Express Company, Plant's first company.
images.alt: The Henry Bradley Plant Memorial Fountain and its statue named "Transportation." It is located at the entrance to Plant Park. The ship and train in the sculpture represent Plant's system of railroads and steamship lines. The eagle holding the strongbox is the logo of The Southern Express Company, Plant's first company.

images.caption: Directly across from the front entrance of the Henry B. Plant Museum (originally known as the Tampa Bay Hotel), and within a traffic circle along the cobblestone driveway within the University of Tampa is an elaborate water fountain bearing the full name of the original founder of the Tampa Bay Hotel, as well as the Savannah, Florida and Western Railway ("Plant System"), a predecessor to the Atlantic Coast Line Railroad. This is one of the rare instances where Plant's full name is on display.
images.alt: Directly across from the front entrance of the Henry B. Plant Museum (originally known as the Tampa Bay Hotel), and within a traffic circle along the cobblestone driveway within the University of Tampa is an elaborate water fountain bearing the full name of the original founder of the Tampa Bay Hotel, as well as the Savannah, Florida and Western Railway ("Plant System"), a predecessor to the Atlantic Coast Line Railroad. This is one of the rare instances where Plant's full name is on display.
